clamp.nl: Take the input value x and compare it with the lower and upper bounds. If x is smaller than the lower bound, return the lower bound. Otherwise, if x is larger than the upper bound, return the upper bound. If neither condition holds, return x unchanged.
clamp.pseudo:
IF x < lo THEN
    RETURN lo
ELSE IF x > hi THEN
    RETURN hi
ELSE
    RETURN x
END IF

gcd.nl: Start with a and b. While b is not zero, compute the remainder of a divided by b, replace a with b, and replace b with that remainder. When b reaches zero, return a as the greatest common divisor.
gcd.pseudo:
WHILE b != 0 DO
    remainder <- a MOD b
    a <- b
    b <- remainder
END WHILE
RETURN a

fib.nl: Initialize a to zero and b to one. Repeat the update n times. On each iteration, replace a with the old value of b and replace b with the sum of the old a and b. After the loop, return a.
fib.pseudo:
a <- 0
b <- 1
FOR i FROM 0 TO n-1 DO
    next <- a + b
    a <- b
    b <- next
END FOR
RETURN a

is_prime.nl: If n is below two, return false. Otherwise initialize d to two. While d squared is no greater than n, test whether d divides n exactly. If it does, return false; otherwise increment d and continue. If no divisor is found, return true.
is_prime.pseudo:
IF n < 2 THEN RETURN FALSE
d <- 2
WHILE d*d <= n DO
    IF n MOD d == 0 THEN RETURN FALSE
    d <- d + 1
END WHILE
RETURN TRUE

binary_search.nl: Initialize lo to the first index and hi to the last index. While lo does not pass hi, compute the midpoint. If the midpoint value equals the target, return the midpoint. If it is smaller than the target, move lo just above the midpoint; otherwise move hi just below it. Return minus one if the search interval becomes empty.
binary_search.pseudo:
lo <- 0
hi <- LENGTH(xs)-1
WHILE lo <= hi DO
    mid <- FLOOR((lo+hi)/2)
    IF xs[mid] == target THEN RETURN mid
    IF xs[mid] < target THEN
        lo <- mid + 1
    ELSE
        hi <- mid - 1
    END IF
END WHILE
RETURN -1

prefix_sums.nl: Create an empty output list and initialize the running total to zero. Scan the input from left to right. For each value, add it to the running total and append the updated total to the output list. Return the completed list.
prefix_sums.pseudo:
out <- EMPTY LIST
total <- 0
FOR EACH x IN xs DO
    total <- total + x
    APPEND total TO out
END FOR
RETURN out
prefix_sums.code:
def prefix_sums(xs):
    out = []
    total = 0
    for x in xs:
        total += x
        out.append(total)
    return out

count_vowels.nl: Initialize the count to zero. Convert the string to lowercase and scan its characters. For each character, if it belongs to the vowel set, increment the count. Return the final count.
count_vowels.pseudo:
count <- 0
FOR EACH ch IN LOWERCASE(s) DO
    IF ch IN {a,e,i,o,u} THEN
        count <- count + 1
    END IF
END FOR
RETURN count

merge_sorted.nl: Initialize indices i and j at zero and create an empty output list. While both input lists still contain unconsumed values, compare their current values, append the smaller one, and advance the corresponding index. Then append every remaining value from the unfinished list. Return the merged output.
merge_sorted.pseudo:
i <- 0
j <- 0
out <- EMPTY LIST
WHILE i < LENGTH(a) AND j < LENGTH(b) DO
    IF a[i] <= b[j] THEN
        APPEND a[i] TO out
        i <- i + 1
    ELSE
        APPEND b[j] TO out
        j <- j + 1
    END IF
END WHILE
WHILE i < LENGTH(a) DO APPEND a[i] TO out; i <- i + 1 END WHILE
WHILE j < LENGTH(b) DO APPEND b[j] TO out; j <- j + 1 END WHILE
RETURN out

run_count.nl: If the string is empty, return zero. Otherwise initialize the run count to one. Scan from the second character onward. Whenever the current character differs from the previous character, increment the count. Return the final count.
run_count.pseudo:
IF LENGTH(s) == 0 THEN RETURN 0
count <- 1
FOR i FROM 1 TO LENGTH(s)-1 DO
    IF s[i] != s[i-1] THEN
        count <- count + 1
    END IF
END FOR
RETURN count

sum_positive.nl: Initialize a running total to zero. Visit each value in the input list. If the value is positive, add it to the running total. After all values have been examined, return the total.
sum_positive.pseudo:
total <- 0
FOR EACH x IN xs DO
    IF x > 0 THEN
        total <- total + x
    END IF
END FOR
RETURN total
